evidence: src/invoice/invoice.entity.ts: `@Entity('invoices')` on class InvoiceEntity maps the domain class to the database table 'invoices'. Table mapping is persistence work and belongs in infrastructure.
src/invoice/invoice.entity.ts: `@PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') id!: string;` sets how the database generates the key. That is persistence work and belongs in infrastructure.
src/invoice/invoice.entity.ts: `@Column() orderId!: string;` and `@Column() amount!: number;` map fields to columns. Column mapping is persistence work and belongs in infrastructure.
src/invoice/invoice.entity.ts: `hasId()` checks whether the database has assigned an id (persistence state). It is not a domain invariant, and the class has no other business behaviour.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/invoice/invoice.entity.ts is in the domain layer because it matches the **/*.entity.ts pattern. The class InvoiceEntity is also a TypeORM persistence model. @Entity('invoices') ties it to a database table, @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') sets how the database generates the primary key, and @Column() maps each field to a column. Mapping to tables, columns and generated keys is persistence work, which belongs in the infrastructure layer, not in a domain model. The only behaviour in the class is hasId(), and it reflects persistence state: it checks whether the database has assigned an id yet. The file has no business rules, so the class mostly describes database storage rather than domain behaviour. This matches the rubric's fail case of persistence logic in a domain file. Confidence is not full because some projects accept ORM-annotated entities as domain objects, and no ADR text was given to settle that.

violations.message: InvoiceEntity is a domain-layer class that does infrastructure persistence work: @Entity('invoices'), @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') and @Column() map it to a database table, generated key and columns. The ORM mapping should live in an infrastructure persistence model or repository mapping, and the domain model should stay free of storage concerns.
